column1: # Values read off REAL AMIGA HARDWARE, transcribed from the vAmigaTS reference
# photographs.
# This file is the durable part of the vAmigaTS work. The suite is 3.6 GB and
# its references are photographs of a CRT -- neither of which belongs in this
# repository, and neither of which a test can consume. What a test CAN consume
# is the numbers in those photographs, and once they are written down here a
# bench can hold the RTL to them forever without the suite, the disk, the
# camera, or the machine.
# It is the only ground truth this project has. Every other route we have --
# our Icarus benches, the Copperline tables, WinUAE's source read by eye --
# compares one model against another. These are silicon.
# PROVENANCE AND ITS LIMIT. Each row names the photograph it came from. The
# transcription is BY EYE from a JPEG of a CRT: the digits are large and clear,
# but nothing has checked them except a careful read, so a single wrong nibble
# is the failure mode to expect. Anything built on this file should say so, and
# a disagreement with the RTL is worth re-reading the photograph before it is
# worth believing. Re-transcribe rather than "correct" a value that looks wrong.
# SCOPE. vAmigaTS's hardware references are an Amiga 500 (2,967 images), plus
# 18 of an A1200. So these are OCS/ECS values. They do not describe AGA, and
# they do not describe a CD32 -- see docs/vamigats.md on what a real CD32 could
# add here that nothing else can.
# WHAT THE PROBES DO (Agnus/Registers/VPOS/README.md):
#   probe1..probe13  probe VHPOSR at 16 locations and display the result
#   vprobe1..vprobe4 probe VPOSR while crossing the vertical boundary
#                    (vpos changes from $FF to $100)
#   ersy1, ersy2     as the probes, with ERSY set/reset
# 13*16 + 4*16 + 2*16 = 304 -- which is exactly the "304 probe rows" the core
# repo's T7 cites. T7's numbers came from this suite.

# READING NOTES, because the numbers alone do not carry what they mean.
# probe6 -- THE TRANSCRIPTION CHECKS ITSELF, which is worth more than the care
# taken over it: consecutive VHPOSR reads differ by $0A, ten colour clocks, which is
# what one `move.w VHPOSR(a1),d5` plus `move.w d5,(a2)+` costs on a 7 MHz 68000
# reading a custom register. Index 3 to 4 is the line wrap: $FFDC -> $0003, so
# hpos went 220 -> 3. 220 + 10 = 230, and 230 - 227 = 3, which pins the PAL line
# at 227 colour clocks and shows the wrap arithmetic directly. The vpos low byte
# goes $FF -> $00 across the same step.
# All sixteen values step by exactly $0A, and the one that does not is the wrap,
# which closes to the colour clock. A misread nibble would break that chain, so
# the arithmetic is a checksum on the reading. It does not prove the values are
# what the machine showed -- a consistent misreading of the whole column would
# survive it -- but it rules out the single-digit slip that is the likely error.
# vprobe1 -- VPOSR across the vpos $FF -> $100 boundary. Bit 15 (LOF) is 1
# throughout; bit 0 is vpos[8]. Real silicon steps 0 -> 1 cleanly between reads
# 4 and 5: no intermediate value, no glitch, no readback describing a line the
# beam was not on.
# That last point is worth holding onto. The core repo's beam bench found that
# Copperline, at the frame wrap, reassembles VPOSR and VHPOSR into line 256 --
# a line the beam was never on -- while our RTL reassembles to the previous
# line. vprobe1 does not settle that directly, because it reads VPOSR alone and
# not the pair. But it does show the vertical bit itself behaving monotonically
# on hardware, which is the half of the question we can check today.
